newsitem.title: USA: US adj retail sales up 0.5 pct w/e May 31--Redbook.
newsitem.headline: US adj retail sales up 0.5 pct w/e May 31--Redbook.

text.p: U.S. seasonally adjusted retail sales rose 0.5 percent in the period ending May 31 versus April's final estimate, according to the Lynch, Jones & Ryan Inc Redbook Retail Sales Index.
The index rose 5.9 percent compared to the same period a year ago, the report said. Adjusted retail sales rose 6.0 percent in the week ended May 31 compared with the same week a year ago, it said.

The stronger final week, boosted by robust Memorial Day sales, helped maintain the month's averages, but was not sufficient to lift the monthly sales results noticeably, said Howard Eilenberg, a retail analyst at Redbook Research.
"The month was a disappointment to most retailers," said Eilenberg in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
He said many discount retailers have not met their expectations over the past couple of months because poor weather had dampened sales of their seasonal goods.
Apparel sold better in regions where temperatures were warm, such as the Southeast and the West Coast, he said.
"Looking forward into June, if the weather does indeed become seasonal, (retailers) will move those goods before it is time for drastic markdowns," Eilenberg said.
Eilenberg said the year-over-year comparisons for the month ahead should be "relatively easy." He said June sales last year were soft for many retailers.
"The key is Father's Day. After Father's Day, if you haven't gotten rid of your spring merchandise, then you got to start marking it down," Eilenberg added.
